key_insight: Under illustrative routing costs, calibration-selected abstention cut TF-IDF logistic regression’s held-out test cost by 38.1% and reduced wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%.
engineering_relevance: Cost-aware deferral can help determine when automatic ticket routing is preferable to human triage, but confidence calibration alone does not establish routing readiness.
method: Compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four LLMs using zero- and few-shot prompts.
Select routing policies on calibration data under explicit costs, then freeze them for held-out testing.
Assess calibration and discrimination using ECE, correctness AUROC, and tie-aware risk-coverage area.
evidence_signal: On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, the cost reduction had a 95% bootstrap CI of 35.7%–40.4%; on a stratified 1,000-ticket subset, the strongest prompted configuration achieved 0.477 accuracy versus DistilBERT’s 0.879.
watch_item: Results depend on the dataset, prompts, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; this framework is not universal deployment certification.
paper_title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
